findings.title: 'No order of different instruments inside a second is observable' is not demonstrated for SENSEX; the embedded nanosecond time may be comparable across SENSEX instruments
findings.evidence: [RAW] SENSEX same-second adjacent pairs of DIFFERENT instruments: embedded ns increasing with file order 6,482, decreasing 965 (87 percent agreement); same instrument: increasing 2,202, decreasing 28, equal 76 (98.7 percent). Day level 993 decreases in 21,483 adjacent pairs. The project never tested whether the ns is a venue-wide clock; the statement is absolute in docs/ORDERING_SEMANTICS.md. NIFTY ids are per contract (22 ids shared by different instruments; 6,392 day-level decreases in file order). Consequence for results is nil (second-end state is invariant regardless), but the claim 'none is observable' is stronger than the evidence.
findings.fix: Weaken to 'the project does not use any cross-instrument order; it is not shown whether the SENSEX embedded time orders different instruments'.

findings.title: Inclusive 'gap <= g' on whole seconds links pairs whose true gap exceeds g; '1,214 / 840 / ...' counts one direction only
findings.evidence: [RAW] SENSEX (embedded ns): of C1 links at reported gap exactly g, true ns gap > g for 157/340 (g=2), 103/290 (5), 18/45 (10), 7/12 (30), 6/11 (60); no non-link at reported gap g+1 has a true gap <= g. So the inclusive rule behaves as 'true gap < g+1' and the exclusive rule as 'true gap < g'; neither is the stated 'gap <= g seconds'. The exclusive-only batch counts 1,214/840/153/50/63 reproduced exactly [RAW]; they are batches present only in the exclusive view; the NET change in batch count is +661/+441/+79/+25/+33 (= pairs at exactly g) and the inclusive-only batches are 553/399/74/25/30. SENSEX epoch is round-half-up of the embedded ns (only row 8079 inconsistent).
findings.fix: State the whole-second boundary semantics explicitly in M2F_METHODOLOGY_LIMITATIONS section 7 and describe the exclusive sensitivity as 'batches only in the exclusive view (net +661 ... )'.

findings.evidence: [IMPL-synthetic via my partition function] parents A(first 10,last 100), B(10,11), C(50,60), g=30: tie order A,B gives {A,B},{C}; B,A gives {A,B,C}. [RAW] 60 random tie-breaks among equal-first-second parents: C2 batch count 7,126-7,127 (2 s), 3,776-3,777 (5 s), 3,064-3,065 (10 s), constant at 30/60 s; C1 constant (7,127/3,777/3,065/2,171/1,502). Documented in limitations section 7 (Low); noted here because ORDERING_SEMANTICS says the cross-parent serialization carries no claim.
findings.fix: Cross-reference the C2 tie-break sensitivity from ORDERING_SEMANTICS.

findings.title: Parent-level same-second flip can be produced by other parents' fills; 3 of the 26 baseline flips are not attributable to the named parent
findings.evidence: [RAW] baseline 26 parent-level groups: 3 where the parent's own net quantity alone only reaches zero (PE23200 parent 11747186 rows 27906/27916; CE24600 parent 11747185 rows 27908/27917; parent s_22084429338804 rows 33690-33717); hybrid: 0 of 22. Hence the 26 vs 22 gap is an order artefact. On this ledger every one of the 23 baseline per-fill crossings lies inside a parent-level flip group (per-fill is a subset in the data, although not in general). [IMPL-synthetic pe.reversals] inv +5; parent A buys 1, parent B sells 11, parent A buys 1: counts per-fill 1, parent-level 2 (A: +5 to -4 although A only bought; B: +6 to -5): one crossing counted twice. Order dependence: same fills, B-then-A gives 1/1, A-then-B 0/0. Two fills of one parent (+10 to 0 to -10): per-fill 0, parent-level 1. All of this is within the documented caveats; the definitions are unambiguous and all four published counts were reproduced.
findings.reproduce: python3 item2_reversals.py; python3 item2b_attribution.py; python3 counterexamples_ab.py
findings.fix: Optionally add an 'attributable to the parent alone' count next to the parent-level count (3 / 26 baseline, 0 / 22 hybrid).

findings.title: The price-scrambling invariance test cannot see price information read from outside the ledger's px_fill column, and conflates 'rule changed' with 'price dependent'
findings.evidence: [IMPL] scratch copies (never in the repo). Mutant A: CT1 re-ranked by the highest RAW-CSV first-fill price, delivered outputs regenerated with the mutant: tests/test_decision_a.py::test_case_selection_is_invariant_under_upstream_price_scrambling PASSES (188 s); the non-slow pins then fail only because the delivered files changed. Mutant B: same ranking using fills.tsv exec_price_paise (the path the scrambling perturbs): test FAILS (killed). Selection code reads no price column (columns read listed in item4_cases_result.json) and wing/body prices appear only as output columns, so the price-free claim holds for the committed code. 'Outcome-free' means P&L-free: selection conditions on terminal status (CLOSED / expired) and lifecycle shape.
findings.reproduce: python3 item4b_make_mutants.py <scratch> <worktree>; run the slow test inside each scratch portfolio_engine (see REVIEW.md section 4)
findings.fix: Document the test as 'ledger px_fill only'; optionally also scramble px_order_avg/px_limit and make the mirror read a scrambled raw CSV copy; compare mutants against a regenerated baseline rather than the delivered JSON.
